          Overview

          The interfaces of vaxpunk's executive and the PAL below it, as code written against them sees them. Every entry is read from the sources by cargo run -p apidoc: the comment above each routine and macro, the system service vector, and the tables of DESIGN-0001. How the pieces fit is in DESIGN-0001 (the PAL) and DESIGN-0002 (the executive).

          Press / to search. Every name in the text links to its entry. Status lists the condition values found in a routine's code and in what it calls whose failure it passes on. A Limit is a deliberate shortcut, with the way past it.

          TagHow it is called
          ServiceSYS$name with CALLS or CALLG, or the $name_S macro; CHMK, or for $CMEXEC CHME, takes it to the executive
          CALLCALLS or CALLG: arguments in the argument list at AP, status in R0, RET
          JSBJSB or BSBW: arguments and results in registers, RSB
          Handleran SCB vector: the PAL delivers an interrupt, an exception or CHMx to it; it ends with REI
          PALa privileged VAX instruction, or CALL_PAL; vmacro compiles it into svc #0
          Macroa macro from a .LIBRARY; Definitions macros define symbols

          1System services

          Called from any mode with CALLS or CALLG to SYS$name, which is in syssrv.mar, or with the $name_S macros of starlet.mlb. Programs run in user mode, and SYS$name is in the vector, a page user mode may run. A service called with fewer arguments than it takes returns SS$_INSFARG, and one with an argument list or an address its caller's mode can't reach SS$_ACCVIO.

          1.1Process control

          15 of 19 implemented.

          $CREPRC

          Serviceroottask/exec/process.mar:193
          Format
          SYS$CREPRC pidadr, image, input, output, error, prvadr, quota, prcnam, baspri, uic, mbxunt, stsflg
          Macro
          $CREPRC_S PIDADR=0, IMAGE=0, INPUT=0, OUTPUT=0, ERROR=0, PRVADR=0, QUOTA=0, PRCNAM=0, BASPRI=#2, UIC=#0, MBXUNT=#0, STSFLG=#0
          Dispatch
          CHMK #0 to EXE$CMODKRNL, which calls EXE$CREPRC with at least 12 arguments
          Description

          Makes a process that runs image, called prcnam, at priority baspri, and puts its PID in pidadr. input, output and error, if given, are the equivalence strings of its process-permanent logical names SYS$INPUT, SYS$OUTPUT and SYS$ERROR; SS$_BADPARAM for one that is empty or longer than 255. It starts in its creator's default directory. The other arguments are ignored: there is no privilege, quota or UIC yet.

          Status
          SS$_NORMAL SS$_ACCVIO SS$_BADPARAM SS$_EXQUOTA SS$_DUPLNAM SS$_INSFARG SS$_INSFMEM SS$_IVLOGNAM
          Calls
          EXE$PROBER_DSC EXE$ALONONPAGED LNM$CREATE EXE$NAMPID SCH$MAKECOM EXE$DEANONPGDSIZ LNM$DELTBL
          PAL calls
          PROBEW MFPR_IPL MTPR_IPL
          Data
          SCH$GL_CURPCB SCH$GL_PCBVEC SCH$GL_SEQ SGN$GW_QUANTUM

          $DELPRC

          Serviceroottask/exec/process.mar:719
          Format
          SYS$DELPRC pidadr, prcnam
          Macro
          $DELPRC_S PIDADR=0, PRCNAM=0
          Dispatch
          CHMK #1 to EXE$CMODKRNL, which calls EXE$DELPRC with at least 2 arguments
          Description

          Deletes a process, the current one if none is named. Another one's P0 and P1 aren't the current process's, so it runs itself down, in a kernel mode AST, DELKAST, which ends its wait or suspension; it leaves its slot at once, so no one finds it any more. SS$_INSFMEM if there is no pool for the AST.

          Status
          SS$_NORMAL SS$_ACCVIO SS$_NOPRIV SS$_INSFARG SS$_INSFMEM SS$_IVLOGNAM SS$_NONEXPR
          Calls

          PAL calls

          Data

          $EXIT

          Serviceroottask/exec/process.mar:592
          Format
          SYS$EXIT code
          Macro
          $EXIT_S CODE=#1
          Dispatch
          CHMK #2 to EXE$CMODKRNL, which calls EXE$EXIT with at least 1 arguments
          Description

          Ends the image. In a process with a command interpreter, it runs the image down and calls the command interpreter with code. In one without, the image's end is the process's: it is deleted, and a failure status is reported on the console, as a command interpreter would. Doesn't return.

          $GETJPI

          Serviceroottask/exec/getjpi.mar:64
          Format
          SYS$GETJPI efn, pidadr, prcnam, itmlst, iosb, astadr, astprm
          Macro

          Dispatch
          CHMK #12 to EXE$CMODKRNL, which calls EXE$GETJPI with at least 7 arguments
          Description

          Returns what the item list asks about a process: the one pidadr or prcnam names, as $WAKE's, or the next one of a wildcard scan if pidadr points at a negative number, -1 to start. Clears the event flag, then sets it, and writes SS$_NORMAL in the IOSB's first word, if there is one. SS$_NONEXPR for a process that isn't there, SS$_NOMOREPROC past the scan's last, SS$_BADPARAM for an item code it doesn't know.

          $ASTEXIT

          Serviceroottask/exec/astdel.mar:249
          Format
          SYS$ASTEXIT
          Dispatch
          CHMK #40 to EXE$CMODKRNL, which calls EXE$ASTEXIT with at least 0 arguments
          Description

          Ends the AST routine that runs, the one delivered last: puts the kernel stack back to where EXE$ASTDEL left it, which delivers the next AST or returns to what the routine interrupted. EXE$ASTDISP calls it when the routine returns. With no AST routine running, it returns SS$_NORMAL and does nothing.

          2Executive routines

          Routines and data of EXEC.EXE, by module. Programs link against SYS.STB, so kernel-mode code reaches every global here directly. The system services' own routines, EXE$name, are in chapter 1; local routines can only be called from their own module.

          2.1ASTDEL Asynchronous system traps

          roottask/exec/astdel.mar:1

          An AST is a call a process gets in one of its access modes, on top of whatever it was doing there, as on VMS (docs/adr/0011-asts-on-the-kernel-stack.md). SCH$QAST puts an AST control block on the process's AST queue, by mode, kernel's first, and keeps the HWPCB's ASTSR, a bit per mode with an ACB queued, and ASTEN, a bit per mode whose ASTs may be delivered: those $SETAST enabled, less those whose AST routine runs. The PAL requests the AST delivery interrupt, at IPL$_ASTDEL, when IPL is below it and a mode with a bit in both is the current mode or an inner one, as the VAX's REI did with ASTLVL. SCH$ASTDEL delivers there, and SCH$WAIT ends a wait to deliver too, in the mode that called the service waiting.

          EXE$ASTDEL calls an AST routine as EXE$CTRLY calls the command interpreter: it saves the registers and IPL on the kernel stack and REIs below them, to EXE$ASTDISP in the AST's mode, which calls the routine and then $ASTEXIT, which puts the stack pointer back and returns.

          SCH$QAST

          JSBroottask/exec/astdel.mar:41
          Linkage
          JSB G^SCH$QAST; arguments in registers, returns with RSB
          Description

          R5 = an ACB, its mode and PID set. Queues it to the process, after its ACBs of that mode and the inner ones, and ends its wait, if it waits, so that it can deliver the AST. If the process is gone, frees the ACB. R0 = SS$_NORMAL or SS$_NONEXPR.

          2.2EVENT Event flag services

          roottask/exec/event.mar:1

          Each process has 128 event flags in four clusters of 32. Clusters 0 and 1 (flags 0-63) are its own, local. Clusters 2 and 3 (64-127) are common: $ASCEFC associates each with a common event block, a named cluster that every process associated with it shares, which is how processes synchronize with each other. A process waiting for flags is in the LEF state for local ones and in the CEB's wait queue, state CEF, for common ones; $SETEF wakes those whose wait it satisfies.

          SCH$GETEFC

          JSBroottask/exec/event.mar:30

          R3 = an event flag number, R4 = a PCB. Finds its cluster: R1 = the address of the cluster's flags, R2 = the flag's bit in them, R5 = the cluster number. R0 = SS$_NORMAL, SS$_ILLEFC or SS$_UNASEFC.

          2.3EXEC The executive's start, and the swapper

          roottask/exec/exec.mar:1

          The root task, the PAL, starts EXEC.EXE as a task of its own, in kernel mode at IPL 31, with R11 pointing at the restart parameter block (docs/design/0001-pal-interface.md). EXEC$START sets up the system control block, memory, the scheduler, the system time and the console, mounts the system disk, defines the system's logical names for it, starts the console's process, SYSTEM, which runs DCL, and becomes the swapper, process 1, which deletes what deleted processes leave behind (docs/design/0002-executive-processes.md). When SYSTEM is deleted, at LOGOUT, the swapper halts, and the PAL powers the machine off.

          Description

          2.4F11 Files-11 ODS-2 volumes: mounting them, reading and writing blocks

          roottask/exec/f11.mar:1

          Each disk has a VCB: DKA0:, the system disk, a Files-11 ODS-2 volume (ods/docs/) that the PAL reads a block at a time with READLBLK; DKB0:, the data disk, which the PAL also writes, with WRITELBLK; and MDA0:, the ramdisk (mddriver.mar). The file system can write the last two. DK$FDT is their driver, for $QIO's reads and writes by LBN. FIL$MOUNT mounts a volume: it reads the home block and keeps the index file's header, through which every other file's header is found. The rest reads what VMS's XQP reads: a file's header by its number, its blocks through the header's map, and a directory's records, with wildcards. f11wrt.mar writes them. RMS (rms.mar) and the image activator call them at IPL$_SYNCH, which keeps their buffers, and F11$GL_VCB, the volume they work on, to one caller at a time.

          Limit. no extension headers, so a file's map is what its one header holds; DKA0:'s and DKB0:'s I/O waits for the device, at IPL$_SYNCH.

          2.5F11WRT Files-11 writes: headers, blocks, directories, INITIALIZE

          roottask/exec/f11wrt.mar:1

          What VMS's XQP does when files are written, on F11$GL_VCB's volume (f11.mar), which must be on a disk that can be written, DKB0: or MDA0:: a new file gets a header from the index file bitmap, blocks from the storage bitmap (ods/docs/bitmap.md), with a map pointer for each run of them, and an entry in a directory (ods/docs/directory.md); deleting it gives all three back. FIL$INIT, which $INIT_VOL calls, writes an empty volume, laid out as INITIALIZE does (ods/docs/initialize.md). RMS (rms.mar) calls these at IPL$_SYNCH, as it calls f11.mar's.

          Limit. a cluster is a block, and the bitmaps are a block each, so a volume has at most 4096 blocks and 4096 files; the index file isn't extended, so a volume has the headers INITIALIZE made room for; map pointers are format 2, and a directory is rewritten whole on each change, so a version is entered in the first record with its name.

          2.7GETJPI $GETJPI and $GETSYI: about the processes and the system

          roottask/exec/getjpi.mar:1

          A program asks about a process with $GETJPI, and about the system with $GETSYI, as on VMS, with VMS's item codes (starlet.mlb's $JPIDEF and $SYIDEF) in an item list as $GETDVI's. $GETJPI's pidadr pointing at -1 starts a wildcard scan: each call returns the next process, keeping where the scan is in that longword, until SS$_NOMOREPROC; SHOW SYSTEM lists the processes so. A table says, for each item code, how big the value is and where: at an offset in the PCB, or at an address.

          Limit. done at once, no AST; no CPU times, quotas or counts, as nothing keeps them, and no cluster, so $GETSYI's csidadr and nodename are ignored.

          2.8LNM Logical names

          roottask/exec/lnm.mar:1

          A logical name stands for a string, its equivalence: SYS$INPUT for _OPA0:. $CRELNM makes one in a logical name table, $DELLNM deletes it, and $TRNLNM translates it; $ASSIGN translates a device name with LNM$TRNLOG (docs/design/0002-executive-processes.md). There are two tables: each process's own, LNM$PROCESS_TABLE, a queue in its PCB, which goes with the process, and every process's, LNM$SYSTEM_TABLE. Services name a table by that name, or LNM$PROCESS or LNM$SYSTEM, or LNM$FILE_DEV: for $TRNLNM the process's table and then the system's, for the others the process's. Each name is a logical name block from pool, and the tables are synchronized at IPL$_SYNCH.

          Limit. one equivalence string per name, no access modes, attributes, job or group tables, or tables of one's own; VMS's logical name directories, hash table and mutex replace this.

          2.9MDDRIVER MDA0:, a ramdisk, as DECram's

          roottask/exec/mddriver.mar:1

          MDA0: is a disk in memory, as DECram's MDDRIVER made one on VMS: its blocks are pages of S0 from MD_VA, which the first INITIALIZE of MDA0: makes ($INIT_VOL, f11wrt.mar) and every later one makes afresh, zeroed. Until then the device is offline. Reads and writes are copies, at once: the file system (f11.mar) calls MD$IO where it would call the PAL for DKA0:. The pages are the system's, so the volume outlives the processes that wrote it, but not the system.

          Limit. a fixed size, MD$GL_BLOCKS; DECram's INITIALIZE/SIZE when DCL has qualifiers.

          2.10MEMORY Memory management: pages, pool and the memory services

          roottask/exec/memory.mar:1

          The PAL gives the executive physical pages, numbered by PFN, and maps one at an address when the executive writes a PTE with WRPTE. The executive owns the PFN database, here a list of free PFNs, and decides what goes where (docs/design/0002-executive-processes.md). P0 and P1 are each process's own; a PTE written there is the current process's:

            ^X00010000  P0: the process's image, then its $EXPREG pages
  ^X40010000  S0, every process's: EXEC.EXE
  ^X48000000  nonpaged pool: PCBs, kernel stacks, common event blocks,
              timer queue entries, logical names
  ^X4FFF0000  the RPB
  ^X50000000  MDA0:'s blocks, the ramdisk's, once INITIALIZE makes them
  ^X5FFF0000  the boot stack's top
  ^X60000000  P1: the process's $CRETVA pages
  ^X7FF00000  its command interpreter, if it has one, then its mode stacks

          The PFN database and the pool are synchronized at IPL$_SYNCH.

          2.11PROCESS Process creation, deletion and control

          roottask/exec/process.mar:1

          A process is a PCB and a kernel stack in S0, an image and stacks in its own P0 and P1, and the threads the PAL makes for it: the first time the scheduler switches to the process's HWPCB, and the first time it enters each outer mode. $CREPRC builds the PCB and a kernel stack holding the frame REI pops, which starts the process at EXE$PROCSTRT, in kernel mode at IPL 0. There it activates its image from the system disk and REIs to user mode, which calls the image; when the image returns, or calls $EXIT, the process is deleted, as a VMS process is when its image exits and it has no command interpreter.

          An image linked in P1 is a command interpreter: it is activated there and called in supervisor mode, and stays. It runs images with $IMGACT, and when one exits, the process runs it down and calls the command interpreter again (docs/design/0002-executive-processes.md). CTRL/Y stops the image where it is and calls the command interpreter on top of it, and $CONTINUE goes back to it (ADR-0010).

          2.12QIO Channels, I/O request packets and their completion

          roottask/exec/qio.mar:1

          A process does I/O as on VMS (docs/adr/0013-qio-irps-and-drivers.md): $ASSIGN gives it a channel to a device, named so or by a logical name, and $QIO hands a request on it to the device's driver, through the device's UCB. The driver's FDT routine makes an I/O request packet, IOC$ALLOCIRP, and does the I/O at once or queues the IRP on the UCB. Either way it ends with IOC$REQCOM, which queues the IRP to its process as a kernel mode AST, IOC$POST: there the data, the I/O status block and the event flag are written, and the caller's AST queued. $QIOW waits for that. The drivers: the console's, ttdriver.mar, and the disks', DK$FDT in f11.mar.

          IOC$TRNDEVNAM

          JSBroottask/exec/qio.mar:103
          Linkage
          JSB G^IOC$TRNDEVNAM; arguments in registers, returns with RSB
          Description

          R2 = a device name's length, R3 = its address. Translates it as $ASSIGN does: as a logical name, without its colon, in LNM$FILE_DEV, and what it translates to, up to LNM$C_MAXDEPTH times, until a name starts with an underscore, which is dropped, or doesn't translate. R2 and R3 = the name it ends with, in the logical name's block if it is an equivalence. IPL$_SYNCH, which keeps that.

          Registers
          Uses R0, R1, R5-R7.
          Calls
          LNM$TRNLOG
          Called by
          EXE$GETDVI EXE$ASSIGN

          2.13RMS Record Management Services: files on Files-11 volumes

          roottask/exec/rms.mar:1

          A program reads and writes files as on VMS: a FAB names a file and a RAB reads or writes its records, with $OPEN or $CREATE, $CONNECT, $GET or $PUT, $DISCONNECT and $CLOSE; $ERASE deletes one, and $PARSE and $SEARCH find the files a specification with wildcards names, into a NAM block (starlet.mlb's $FABDEF, $RABDEF, $NAMDEF, with VMS's layouts). A specification is [dev:][[dir.dir...]]name.type;ver: what it leaves out comes from the FAB's default specification, then from SYS$DISK: and the process's default directory, which $SETDDIR sets. A device may be a logical name, SYS$SYSTEM:, which stands for some of the parts: those the specification gives win. The device is DKA0:, the system disk, or MDA0:, the ramdisk, with a volume mounted on it, which f11.mar reads and f11wrt.mar writes.

          $OPEN reads the file's header into an IFAB, a block of pool, which the process's PCB holds by IFI, the index $OPEN puts in FAB$W_IFI; $CONNECT puts the same index in RAB$W_ISI. $GET reads sequential files' VAR and FIX records, a block at a time. $CREATE makes a new file, a version above the highest there is unless the specification gives one, with the FAB's record attributes and allocation, and $PUT appends records to it, a block at a time, extending it as it fills; $CLOSE writes its last block and its end of file. An image's files close when it exits, those its command interpreter opened when the process does.

          Limit. the services run in kernel mode at IPL$_SYNCH, which keeps the file system's buffers to one caller; VMS's RMS runs in executive mode, in the process's own P1. One stream per file; $OPEN only reads and $PUT only appends to a file $CREATE made; no file sharing or locking, search lists or concealed devices, ASTs or completion routines, and $SEARCH finds its place again by counting the matches it skips.

R0 = RMS$_NORMAL, RMS$_SYN, RMS$_DEV, RMS$_DIR, RMS$_FNM, RMS$_VER, RMS$_DNF, or the disk's error. The strings must be readable.

          2.14SCHED The scheduler

          roottask/exec/sched.mar:1

          Processes are threads in the executive's address space, and only one of them runs at a time: the current process, SCH$GL_CURPCB. The others wait in a state queue: one per priority for those that are computable (COM), one per wait state for the rest (docs/design/0002-executive-processes.md). The scheduler's database is synchronized at IPL$_SYNCH, as on a uniprocessor VMS: below it, the reschedule interrupt at IPL$_RESCHED may take the CPU away; at or above it, nothing does.

          A process gives up the CPU by calling SCH$SCHED, which picks the highest computable process and hands it the CPU with SWPCTX. The PAL keeps each process's registers in its own thread, so the switch saves nothing: the process leaving waits inside its SWPCTX until the CPU comes back to it.

          The interval timer takes the CPU from a process whose quantum is up, if another computable one has its priority or a higher one: SCH$QEND, round robin within a priority.

          2.15SYSSRV The system service vector, the change mode dispatchers

          roottask/exec/syssrv.mar:1

          A program calls a system service as on VMS, with CALLS or CALLG to SYS$name, or with the $name_S macros in starlet.mlb. SYS$name changes mode to kernel with CHMK and the service's code; the PAL delivers the CHMK through the SCB to EXE$CMODKRNL, which checks the argument list and calls the service's EXE$name routine with it, then REIs with its status in R0. $CMEXEC changes mode to executive instead, with CHME, which EXE$CMODEXEC serves.

          Programs run in user mode, and command interpreters in supervisor mode, so SYS$name, EXE$CMODEXEC, and EXE$USRSTART and EXE$CLISTART, where a process enters those modes, are in a page of their own, the vector, which EXEC$START makes user readable: code an outer mode may run, as VMS's system service vector is.

          Services that aren't implemented yet are stubs that return SS$_ILLSER. An access violation or a reserved instruction in an outer mode ends the process.

          2.16TIMESCHDL The interval timer, the system time and the timer queue

          roottask/exec/timeschdl.mar:1

          The PAL delivers the interval timer interrupt every 10 ms, at IPL$_HWCLK, wherever the current process is (docs/adr/0004-interval-timer-is-a-pal-thread.md). As on VMS, the hardware clock's handler does as little as it can: it advances the system time, charges the tick to the current process's quantum and, when the quantum is up or the first timer queue entry is due, requests the software timer interrupt, whose handler does the rest at a lower IPL (docs/design/0002-executive-processes.md).

          Times are VMS's: a quadword of 100 ns units since 17-Nov-1858 00:00, or, negative, a delta from now. The timer queue holds what $SETIMR and $SCHDWK asked for, in the order it is due. It is synchronized at IPL$_SYNCH; the system time, and EXE$GQ_1ST_TIME, which the hardware clock's handler reads, at IPL$_HWCLK.

          EXE$INITTIM

          JSBroottask/exec/timeschdl.mar:54

          Description

          Makes the timer queue empty and sets the system time, and EXE$GQ_BOOTTIME, from the RTC's, which the PAL put in the RPB. IPL 31.

          Limit. EMUL is signed, so the RTC's seconds work until 2038.

          2.17TTDRIVER The console's terminal driver

          roottask/exec/ttdriver.mar:1

          OPA0:, the console, is a terminal, and this is its driver (docs/adr/0013-qio-irps-and-drivers.md). $QIO calls TT$FDT, which writes a buffer at once, and queues a read on the console's UCB, in an IRP that holds its prompt and the line read.

          What the console receives, its receive interrupt puts in the type-ahead buffer, and requests the IPL$_IOPOST software interrupt, where the read at the head of the queue takes the characters, echoing and editing the line, or recalling one read before, up to a carriage return or CTRL/Z, or a key at a time with IO$M_NOFILTR. A read that ends is completed, and the next one writes its prompt and goes on from there. What is typed while no read is queued waits in the buffer. CTRL/Y empties the buffer instead, ends the reads of the process whose image it stops with SS$_CONTROLY, and stops the image, so that the console's command interpreter prompts (ADR-0010).

          Limit. one terminal, so the line being read is kept here, not in its UCB; output is written a buffer at a time at IPL$_SYNCH, waiting for the console, so lines don't mix.

          TT$FDT

          JSBroottask/exec/ttdriver.mar:85
          Linkage
          JSB G^TT$FDT; arguments in registers, returns with RSB
          Description

          The console's FDT routine, which $QIO calls. R4 = the current PCB, R5 = OPA0:'s UCB, AP = $QIO's arguments. Writes p2 bytes at p1, for IO$_WRITEVBLK, IO$_WRITELBLK and IO$_WRITEPBLK, and completes the request with the count. Queues a read of a line into them, for IO$_READVBLK, IO$_READLBLK and IO$_READPBLK, and for IO$_READPROMPT once it has written the p6 bytes at p5, without echo for IO$M_NOECHO and a key at a time for IO$M_NOFILTR (EDIT). Its IOSB has the line's length and its terminator, a carriage return or CTRL/Z, and its size, or 0 if the buffer filled. R0 = SS$_NORMAL, SS$_ILLIOFUNC, SS$_ACCVIO, SS$_BADPARAM, or IOC$ALLOCIRP's failure.

          JSB localroottask/exec/ttdriver.mar:224
          Linkage
          BSBW EDIT, from roottask/exec/ttdriver.mar only
          Description

          R0 = a character typed, for the line at R2, R3 bytes, R1 of them read, the cursor at R5, R7 lines back in the recall buffer, R6 = the read's function. Echoes the character and edits the line, as VMS does, in insert mode: the left and right arrows move the cursor, CTRL/H to the line's start and CTRL/E to its end, DEL erases the character before the cursor and CTRL/U all of them. The up arrow or CTRL/B recalls the line read before, again for the one before that, up to RECALL lines, and the down arrow goes back down, to an empty line past the last. Other control characters and escape sequences are dropped. A carriage return ends the line, echoed as CR LF, or CTRL/Z, echoed as *EXIT*. With IO$M_NOECHO nothing is echoed or recalled, and with IO$M_NOFILTR every character but a carriage return goes in the line as it is, so a buffer of one byte reads a key. R0 = the terminator, as in the I/O status block: the character, one byte, if it ended the line, else -1.

          Limit. insert mode only, no CTRL/A for overstrike or CTRL/J; the recall buffer is the console's, every reader's, not DCL's, and has no RECALL command; VMS ends a read with IO$M_NOFILTR at any control character in the terminator mask too.

          2.18CONSOLIO Console output, as VMS's EXE$OUT* routines

          vtools/lib/consolio.mar:1

          The routines VMS's own bugcheck and init code print on the console with, and drivers too: called with JSB, arguments in registers. Like VMS's, they take no lock and don't change IPL; callers who share the console take it first. R11 selects the device on the VAX, 0 for the console; it is ignored, as on Alpha. Link this module with the program: vmacro compiles it. CON$PUTCHAR, the one part that knows the hardware, comes from elsewhere: conputchar.mar under vrun, the executive's own under the PAL.

          3PAL calls

          The executive calls the PAL, the root task, with svc #0: the function code in x7, arguments in x0-x5, the result in x0. MACRO-32 code doesn't write that: vmacro compiles privileged VAX instructions and CALL_PAL into it.

          3.2Calling the PAL

          From DESIGN-0001, Calling the PAL.

          The executive calls the PAL with svc #0:

          RegisterInOut
          x7function codeunchanged
          x0a0, the first argumentv0, the result, if the call has one
          x1-x5a1-a5unchanged
          x6, x8-x30, sp, NZCVnot seen by the PALunchanged

          3.3VAX instructions that are PAL calls

          From DESIGN-0001, How MACRO-32 calls it.

          VAX instructionPAL call
          MTPR src, #PR$_IPLMTPR_IPL, a0 = src
          MFPR #PR$_IPL, dstMFPR_IPL, dst = v0
          MFPR #PR$_PCBB, dstMFPR_PCBB
          MTPR src, #PR$_SCBB, MFPR #PR$_SCBB, dstMTPR_SCBB, MFPR_SCBB
          MTPR src, #PR$_SIRRMTPR_SIRR
          MFPR #PR$_SISR, dstMFPR_SISR
          MTPR src, #PR$_TXDBMTPR_TXDB
          MTPR src, #PR$_RXCS, MFPR #PR$_RXCS, dstMTPR_RXCS, MFPR_RXCS
          MFPR #PR$_RXDB, dstMFPR_RXDB
          CHMK #code, CHME, CHMS, CHMUCHMK, CHME, CHMS, CHMU, R0 = code; R0 isn't kept
          PROBER mode, len, base, PROBEWPROBER, PROBEW, a0 = base, a1 = len, a2 = mode; Z set if v0 is 0, no access
          REIREI
          HALTHALT
          CALL_PAL #codeany call: a0-a5 in R0-R5, v0 in R0, as on Alpha

          3.4What the PAL sets up

          From DESIGN-0001, What the PAL sets up.

          every process shares (Memory):

          AddressWhatProtection
          0x40010000 upEXEC.EXE's sections, at their link addressestheirs
          0x4FFF0000the restart parameter block, one pagekernel write
          0x5FFEC000-0x5FFF0000the boot stack, 16 KBkernel write

          3.5The restart parameter block

          From DESIGN-0001, The restart parameter block.

          $RPBDEF in vtools/lib/lib.mlb, longwords:

          OffsetFieldHolds
          0RPB$L_BASEthe RPB's address
          4RPB$L_PFNCNThow many PFNs the executive has: 0 to PFNCNT - 1
          8RPB$L_FREEPFNthe PFNs below this one hold what the PAL set up
          12RPB$L_BOOTTIMEseconds since 1970 at boot, from QEMU virt's PL031 RTC, which the PAL maps after the UART and reads once
          64RPB$Q_HWPCBthe boot context's HWPCB, 128 bytes

          3.6Page table entries

          From DESIGN-0001, Memory.

          sign-extended longwords reach (ADR-0005):

          RegionAddressesWhose
          P00x00000000-0x3FFFFFFFthe current process's: its image, from 0x10000
          S00x40000000-0x5FFFFFFFthe system's, the same in every process
          P10x60000000-0x7FFFFFFFthe current process's: its stacks, at the top

          A PTE is the VAX's longword ($PTEDEF), with one change:

          BitsFieldMeaning
          31Vvalid: the page is mapped
          30:27PROTthe VAX protection code ($PRTDEF): who may read and write
          25EXECnew: instructions may run from the page; ARM64 has the permission, the VAX had none
          20:0PFNthe page frame

          3.7The interrupt frame

          From DESIGN-0001, Interrupts and exceptions.

          OffsetHolds
          0PC
          8PSL
          16R7
          24the interrupted VAX SP
          32the interrupted ARM64 sp
          40-80x13-x18, vmacro's scratch registers
          88x30

          3.8Faults and HALT

          From DESIGN-0001, Faults and HALT.

          took it:

          EventThe PAL prints
          Page fault%PAL-F-ACCVIO with the address and PC
          Undefined instruction, brk (BPT)%PAL-F-OPCDEC with the PC
          Reserved PAL call, bad WRPTE%PAL-F-OPCDEC with the code, PC, R0 and R1
          Delivery with no vector or stack%PAL-F-NOVEC
          REI without a frame%PAL-F-REI
          HALT%PAL-I-HALT with the PC and R0

          3.9The Alpha OpenVMS calls

          From DESIGN-0001, The Alpha calls.

          Privileged, 0x00-0x3F:

          CodeCallsvaxpunk
          0x00HALTkept, implemented
          0x01, 0x02DRAINA, CFLUSHdropped: seL4 does cache maintenance on frames
          0x03, 0x04LDQP, STQPdropped: the executive has no physical addresses
          0x05SWPCTXchanged, implemented: contexts are threads, made on first switch, deleted by DELCTX
          0x06MFPR_ASNdropped: address space numbers are seL4's
          0x07, 0x08, 0x26, 0x27MTPR_ASTEN, MTPR_ASTSR, MFPR_ASTEN, MFPR_ASTSRchanged: bytes of the HWPCB, which the executive writes and the PAL reads (ADR-0011)
          0x09, 0x0ACSERVE, SWPPALdropped: firmware services
          0x0B, 0x0CMFPR_FEN, MTPR_FENkept, with floating point
          0x0DMTPR_IPIRkept, with more than one CPU
          0x0E, 0x0FMFPR_IPL, MTPR_IPLkept, implemented
          0x10, 0x11MFPR_MCES, MTPR_MCESkept
          0x12MFPR_PCBBkept, implemented
          0x13, 0x14MFPR_PRBR, MTPR_PRBRkept
          0x15MFPR_PTBRdropped: page tables are the PAL's
          0x16, 0x17MFPR_SCBB, MTPR_SCBBkept, implemented
          0x18, 0x19MTPR_SIRR, MFPR_SISRkept, implemented
          0x1A-0x1D, 0x24, 0x25MFPR_TBCHK, MTPR_TBIA, MTPR_TBIAP, MTPR_TBIS, MTPR_TBISD, MTPR_TBISIchanged: WRPTE
          0x1E-0x23MFPR_ESP, MTPR_ESP, MFPR_SSP, MTPR_SSP, MFPR_USP, MTPR_USPkept
          0x29, 0x2AMFPR_VPTB, MTPR_VPTBdropped: no virtual page table
          0x2B, 0x2EMTPR_PERFMON, MTPR_DATFXdropped
          0x30-0x33MFPR_VIRBND, MTPR_VIRBND, MFPR_SYSPTBR, MTPR_SYSPTBRdropped: page tables are the PAL's
          0x3EWTINTkept, implemented: the idle loop waits for an interrupt
          0x3FMFPR_WHAMIkept

          Unprivileged, 0x80-0xBF:

          CodeCallsvaxpunk
          0x80BPTkept; today BPT is brk, an undefined-instruction fault
          0x81BUGCHKkept
          0x82-0x85CHME, CHMK, CHMS, CHMUchanged, implemented: the PAL moves the call to the process's thread for that mode
          0x86IMBkept
          0x87-0x8E, 0x93-0x9A, 0xA2-0xA9INSQHIL ... REMQUEQ/D, the resident formskept; INSQUE and REMQUE are inline code, since one thread runs at a time
          0x8F, 0x90PROBER, PROBEWkept, implemented
          0x91, 0x92RD_PS, REIkept, implemented
          0x9B, 0x9CSWASTEN, WR_PS_SWSWASTEN changed: $SETAST writes ASTEN; WR_PS_SW kept
          0x9DRSCCkept
          0x9E, 0x9FREAD_UNQ, WRITE_UNQdropped: user mode writes TPIDR_EL0 itself
          0xA0, 0xA1AMOVRR, AMOVRMdropped: ARM64 has atomics
          0xAAGENTRAPkept
          0xAECLRFENkept, with floating point

          vaxpunk's own, 0x40-0x7F:

          CodeCallStands in for
          0x40MTPR_TXDBthe VAX console transmit register
          0x41WRPTEwriting a PTE in memory, then MTPR_TBIS
          0x42DELCTXthe PAL's half of deleting a process
          0x43-0x45MTPR_RXCS, MFPR_RXCS, MFPR_RXDBthe VAX console receive registers

          Macro libraries, for .LIBRARY with vasm -I.

          $HWPCBDEF

          Definitionsvtools/lib/lib.mlb:133
          Format
          $HWPCBDEF
          Description

          The hardware PCB the PAL knows a process context by. Quadword aligned. When a context first runs, the PAL pops an INTSTK frame from its KSP, as REI does. Each mode's stack pointer is where the PAL pushes a frame on entering it from an outer mode, and where it saves the stack pointer of a mode it leaves for another. The PAL requests the AST delivery interrupt, at IPL$_ASTDEL, when IPL is below it and a mode bit set in both ASTEN and ASTSR is the current mode's or an inner one's.

          4.2pic.mlb

          vtools/lib/pic.mlb:1

          pic.mlb: macros for position-independent code (docs/linker.md). Use it with .LIBRARY "pic.mlb" and vasm -I vtools/lib.

          $LDADR

          Macrovtools/lib/pic.mlb:8
          Format
          $LDADR REG, SYMBOL, ?SLOT
          Description

          Loads SYMBOL's address into REG, a 64-bit register, from a linkage slot in $LINK$. The code reaches the slot PC-relative; the slot holds the address, which the loader fixes up if the image moves. Each use makes its own slot.

          Expansion
          show
                  .SAVE_PSECT
        .PSECT  $LINK$
SLOT:   .ADDRESS SYMBOL
        .RESTORE_PSECT
        adrp    REG, SLOT
        ldr     REG, [REG, #:lo12:SLOT]

          4.3starlet.mlb

          vtools/lib/starlet.mlb:1

          starlet.mlb: what programs that call system services use, like VMS's STARLET.MLB. Use it with .LIBRARY "starlet.mlb" and vasm -I vtools/lib.

          The _S forms of the system services: each pushes its arguments, last first, and calls SYS$name. A value argument is pushed as written (EFN=#65); an address argument is pushed as an address (PIDADR=PID), or as 0 if it is 0, the default.

          $FAB

          Macrovtools/lib/starlet.mlb:236
          Format
          $FAB FNA=0, FNS=0, DNA=0, DNS=0, NAM=0, FAC=0
          Description

          A FAB, RAB or name block, with the fields given and the rest 0. Lengths are values (FNS=#5 is FNS=5 here), addresses labels.

          Expansion
          show
                  .BYTE   3, 80                   ; BID, BLN
        .WORD   0                       ; IFI
        .LONG   0, 0, 0, 0              ; FOP, STS, STV, ALQ
        .WORD   0                       ; DEQ
        .BYTE   FAC, 0                  ; FAC, SHR
        .LONG   0                       ; CTX
        .BYTE   0, 0, 0, 0              ; RTV, ORG, RAT, RFM
        .LONG   0, 0                    ; JNL, XAB
        .ADDRESS NAM, FNA, DNA
        .BYTE   FNS, DNS
        .BLKB   26                      ; MRS to the end

          $RAB

          Macrovtools/lib/starlet.mlb:250
          Format
          $RAB FAB=0, UBF=0, USZ=0
          Description

          A FAB, RAB or name block, with the fields given and the rest 0. Lengths are values (FNS=#5 is FNS=5 here), addresses labels.

          Documented with $FAB.

          Expansion
          show
                  .BYTE   1, 68                   ; BID, BLN
        .WORD   0                       ; ISI
        .LONG   0, 0, 0                 ; ROP, STS, STV
        .WORD   0, 0, 0, 0              ; RFA, and a word
        .LONG   0                       ; CTX
        .BYTE   0, 0, 0, 0              ; two bytes, RAC, TMO
        .WORD   USZ, 0                  ; USZ, RSZ
        .ADDRESS UBF
        .LONG   0, 0, 0                 ; RBF, RHB, KBF
        .BYTE   0, 0, 0, 0              ; KSZ, KRF, MBF, MBC
        .LONG   0                       ; BKT
        .ADDRESS FAB
        .LONG   0                       ; XAB

          4.4vrun.mlb

          vtools/lib/vrun.mlb:1

          vrun.mlb: macros for programs that run under vrun, one per monitor call (docs/runner-abi.md). Use it with .LIBRARY "vrun.mlb" and vasm -I vtools/lib. A vaxpunk macro library is a text file of .MACRO definitions. vmacro (MACRO-32) can use it too, so expressions avoid << and >>.

          $EXIT

          Macrovtools/lib/vrun.mlb:8
          Format
          $EXIT STATUS=1
          Description

          Ends the run. STATUS is a VMS condition value; the default is SS$_NORMAL.

          Expansion
          show
                  movz    x0, #((STATUS) & ^XFFFF)
        movk    x0, #(((STATUS) / 65536) & ^XFFFF), lsl #16
        svc     #1

          $PUT

          Macrovtools/lib/vrun.mlb:16
          Format
          $PUT TEXT, ?STRING, ?AFTER
          Description

          Writes TEXT to the console. TEXT is written as for .ASCII, for example "Hello"<10>; it goes into $LITERAL$. Uses x0 and x1.

          Expansion
          show
                  .SAVE_PSECT
        .PSECT  $LITERAL$
STRING: .ASCII  TEXT
AFTER:
        .RESTORE_PSECT
        adr     x0, STRING
        mov     x1, #AFTER - STRING
        svc     #2

          $WRITE

          Macrovtools/lib/vrun.mlb:29
          Format
          $WRITE ADDRESS, LENGTH
          Description

          Writes LENGTH bytes from ADDRESS, both registers. Uses x0 and x1, so LENGTH can't be x0.

          Expansion
          show
                  mov     x0, ADDRESS
        mov     x1, LENGTH
        svc     #2

          $DUMP

          Macrovtools/lib/vrun.mlb:36
          Format
          $DUMP
          Description

          Prints every register.

          Expansion
          show
                  svc     #3

          4.5sysexe.mlb

          roottask/sysexe/sysexe.mlb:1

          sysexe.mlb: console output for the system disk's programs, which run in user mode and print with PUT_LINE in lib/print.mar, a line on OPA0: with $QIOW. Each line is written whole, so no other process's comes in between.

          PRINT

          Macroroottask/sysexe/sysexe.mlb:7
          Format
          PRINT TEXT, ?L
          Description

          Writes text and CR LF. Uses R0-R1.

          Expansion
          show
                  .EXTERNAL PUT_LINE
        .SAVE_PSECT LOCAL_BLOCK
        .PSECT  $LITERAL$
L:      .ASCIC  TEXT
        .RESTORE_PSECT
        PUSHAB  L
        CALLS   #1, G^PUT_LINE

          PRINTHEX

          Macroroottask/sysexe/sysexe.mlb:18
          Format
          PRINTHEX TEXT, VALUE, ?L
          Description

          Writes text, value in hex, and CR LF. Uses R0-R1.

          Expansion
          show
                  .EXTERNAL PUT_LINE
        .SAVE_PSECT LOCAL_BLOCK
        .PSECT  $LITERAL$
L:      .ASCIC  TEXT
        .RESTORE_PSECT
        PUSHL   VALUE
        PUSHAB  L
        CALLS   #2, G^PUT_LINE

          EXPECT

          Macroroottask/sysexe/sysexe.mlb:31
          Format
          EXPECT STATUS, N, ?OK
          Description

          Returns 2 * n, an error the executive reports with the process's name, unless R0 is status.

          Expansion
          show
                  CMPL    R0, STATUS
        BEQL    OK
        MOVL    #<N * 2>, R0
        RET
OK:
